meta.title: Game Show
meta.description: Mr. Randoman's Game Show room: choose a Game of Skill or a Game of Luck, play through up to six rounds of trivia, memory and pure luck, and decide after every round whether to bank your prizes or risk them for a better one. It's all or nothing — lose a round and the whole shelf vanishes. The room and its games are the same in both versions, with only a cosmetic difference in how the prize shelf behaves.

prose.heading: Meet Mr. Randoman
prose.text: The Game Show is one of the special rooms that can appear on your adventure path. The host, Randoman (you'll recognize him from the random-trade encounters — he's a WAHEY person), lays out a shelf of six prizes that were pre-rolled for your visit. You pick a category: a Game of Skill (guessing games based on Pokémon knowledge) or a Game of Luck (coin flips and number guessing). A specific game is then chosen for you, and you play through its rounds.

prose.heading: Risk it or bank it
prose.text: Each game runs up to six rounds (Voltorb Flip is three). After every correct round the next prize on the shelf lights up and Randoman asks you to choose: stop now and take the prizes you've earned, or risk it for the bigger prize on offer. The answer options get harder each round — the first round offers four choices, the second five, and so on (3 + the round number). If you ever answer wrong, the game ends immediately and the entire shelf is hidden: it's all or nothing, and you leave empty-handed. Bank it, and you walk up to the shelf and collect your prizes one by one.

prose.heading: Winning big (and what happens if you cheat)
prose.text: Clear all the rounds and the game ends on a high note: every prize is yours, and finishing the Game Show with a perfect run fires a special quest event. One more thing: the prize counter keeps a grudge. Interact with it when there's no active prize — Randoman takes it as cheating, a note appears ('Cheaters never prosper ke ke ke - Randoman'), and an Electrode is sent after you. The battle is treated like a legendary encounter, so it's the one thing in the Game Show you cannot catch.

records.name: Game Show Room
records.description: A special adventure-path room (preview: 'It's a… Game Show?'). Six prize items are rolled for your visit and displayed on a shelf; the host NPC, the Game Show host sprite and the prize counter are placed in the room. The shelf's item sprites behave slightly differently between versions (see the Rewards record).

records.name: Who's that Pokémon?
records.description: A silhouette of a random Pokémon (from the species pool available to your Pokédex, avoiding species shown recently) is displayed, and you pick its name from a list. Carries one in four of the skill-game weight.
records.source: src/rogue_gameshow.c @vanilla L50-108 / @origin/expansion L49-107 (random species selection from the active dex, recently-shown species excluded, 3+round options); data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L194-245 (silhouette + prompt), L98-140 (skill-game selection: random(4), this game is case 0) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: What's that Cry?
records.description: The same silhouette-and-guess format, but the prompt is the Pokémon's cry instead of its sprite. Carries two in four of the skill-game weight, so it's the most common skill game.
records.source: src/rogue_gameshow.c @vanilla L50-108 / @origin/expansion L49-107 (species selection shared with Who's that); data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L248-308 (cry prompt), L98-140 (skill-game selection: random(4), this game is cases 1–2) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Voltorb Flip
records.description: The classic Voltorb Flip board: flip cards and collect all the 2s and 3s without turning over a Voltorb. Three rounds (each round counts as two prizes, and the board difficulty steps up after each clear), one in four of the skill-game weight.
records.source: data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L311-346 (3 rounds, +2 reward counter per round, difficulty level +2) (identical @origin/expansion); data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L98-140 (skill-game selection: random(4), Voltorb Flip is case 3) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Team Trivia (currently disabled)
records.description: A sixth skill game where you answer questions about your own party ('Which of your Pokémon has the highest HP?' and similar). The game is fully scripted with stat-based questions, but the validity check that gates it is hard-coded to fail with a TODO comment, so the game is never actually offered — the random(5) selection branch that would include it is dead code, and the live skill-game pool contains only the three games above (weighted 1/4, 2/4, 1/4).
records.source: src/rogue_gameshow.c @vanilla L163-167 (GameShow_IsTeamTriviaRoundValid hard-coded FALSE with TODO), L179-243 (stat-based trivia question buffers) / @origin/expansion L130-134, L146-210; data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L98-125 (selection: the validity-gated random(5) branch, whose case 4 is dead code), L348-404 (scripted game) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Higher or Lower
records.description: Six rounds of number guessing: a number from 1 to 100 is shown and you guess whether the next random number will be higher or lower. Ties count against you.
records.source: data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L529-607 (Higher or Lower: 6 rounds, random numbers 1–100) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Rounds and escalating options
records.description: Skill and luck games run six rounds (Voltorb Flip three). The silhouette/cry guessing games build their answer list dynamically with 3 + round number options — four choices in round one, nine by round six — so the odds of guessing right drift against you as the shelf fills.
records.source: src/rogue_gameshow.c @vanilla L71-108 / @origin/expansion L70-107 (GameShow_AppendSpeciesMultichoiceOptions: 3 + currentRound options, correct answer included once); data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L191-310 (round loops) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: All-or-nothing rewards
records.description: Each of the six shelf prizes is a distinct pre-rolled item. A correct round lights up the next prize and offers you the choice to stop and collect, or risk it for the next (better) prize. A wrong answer hides the whole shelf — everything you had earned is gone. If you clear every round the game ends automatically, all prizes are collected, and a map-specific quest event is triggered. Item quantities are adjusted by the run's pickup rules when you collect.

differences.vanilla: The prize sprites are physically repositioned every time the shelf updates: lit prizes are snapped back to their shelf spots and hidden prizes are moved off to (0,0), so the shelf visibly reshuffles as the game plays.
differences.ex: Only the visibility of the prize sprites is toggled — the shelf items stay in place and simply appear and disappear.

records.name: The Cheater's Electrode
records.description: The prize counter is wired to a trap: interacting with it while there is no active prize to claim shows a note — 'Cheaters never prosper ke ke ke - Randoman' — and starts a battle against an Electrode. The battle runs through the legendary-battle flow, so the Electrode cannot be caught.
records.source: data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L158-173 (Rogue_Interact_GiveReward: no-prize path → note + Electrode via legendary battle setup) (identical @origin/expansion)
